ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: auth-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 03:43 UTC)
Alerting service: auth
Alert time: 2026-03-26T03:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-03-26T02:00:00Z to 2026-03-26T05:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 3 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-03-26T03:55:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-03-26T03:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check the error rate of auth service around the alert time.)
  Result: M-005: Only 6 points in this range, too few to test for a change; use a wider range.
  [M-005] auth.error_rate_pct from 2026-03-26T03:30:00Z to 2026-03-26T03:55:00Z (6 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.33 max=32.34 mean=21.62 last=32.32; mean=21.62. Only 6 points in this range, too few to test for a change; use a wider range. Notable points: 2026-03-26T03:30:00Z = 0.33 (lowest); 2026-03-26T03:50:00Z = 32.34 (peak); 2026-03-26T03:55:00Z = 32.32 (last).
Step 2: log_search {"end": "2026-03-26T03:46:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "query": "error exception fail", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-03-26T03:40:00Z"} (asked because: Search for error logs in auth service around the alert start time.)

  [L-0283] 2026-03-26T03:40:51Z auth ERROR handler failed: invalid argument in request processing request_id=req-59659a76

Step 3: metrics_query {"end": "2026-03-26T03:55:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-03-26T03:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if auth service db connection pool is exhausted.)
  Result: M-003: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-003] auth.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-03-26T03:00:00Z to 2026-03-26T03:55:00Z (12 points, 5-minute steps): min=25.26 max=31.89 mean=29 last=29.76; mean=29. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-03-26T03:35:00Z = 25.26 (lowest); 2026-03-26T03:40:00Z = 31.89 (peak); 2026-03-26T03:55:00Z = 29.76 (last).
Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-03-26T03:55:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-03-26T03:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if downstream payments service is experiencing high latency.)
  Result: M-042: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-042] payments.latency_p99_ms from 2026-03-26T03:00:00Z to 2026-03-26T03:55:00Z (12 points, 5-minute steps): min=192.81 max=234.95 mean=209.86 last=200.75; mean=209.86. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-03-26T03:00:00Z = 234.95 (peak); 2026-03-26T03:15:00Z = 192.81 (lowest); 2026-03-26T03:55:00Z = 200.75 (last).
Step 5: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "downstream timeout payments service failure mitigation"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook steps for downstream timeout issues.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-13-8 (match score 7.2).
  [R-13-8] DNS resolution failures - Related runbooks (match score 7.2): If connections work but replies are slow, use the downstream dependency timeout runbook. If requests are turned away because healthy servers are overloaded, use the traffic spike runbook instead of this one.
  [R-09-8] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Related runbooks (match score 6.2): If load is uneven across servers while total traffic is normal, use the load balancer runbook. If the extra load is mostly retries after a failure elsewhere, start from the downstream dependency runbook.
  [R-04-1] Downstream dependency timeout - Summary (match score 5.4): A service is failing because something it relies on is slow or not answering. Calls to it run out of time, retries pile on extra load, and the failure spreads upstream to the callers of this service.

Previous hypotheses:
- downstream_timeout: Requests to /api/v1/pay are failing with 500 and 502 status codes alongside high durations, pointing to a possible timeout or failure in a downstream payment or auth dependency. (evidence: L-0285, L-0289, L-0293, L-0298, L-0300, L-0301)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: High request durations and 500/502 errors can be indicative of database connection pool exhaustion slowing down or hanging active requests. (evidence: L-0285, L-0298, L-0300)
